answer: In an agent economy, reputation works like a time-locked vault. Every honest transaction strengthens an agent's bond, but it vests at a fixed, slow pace, like easing open a velvet-lined chest thread by thread. A fresh identity starts at zero trust, so a gale of sybil forges gains no instant credibility: each fake must grind through weeks of capped, low-weight transactions before it matters. Its synthetic signal, a burst of newborn zero-reputation accounts, is priced exactly at what it costs, so spawning dozens is far more expensive than running one honest agent.
